title: I Have No Time to Look at Things...
text:
I have no time to look at things

as I desire.

They slip over my gaze,

and all that I see

are deep corners labeled with radio,

where I read the city so as not to lose time.

This forced haste that inexorably

wants to hand me the world with a small datum.

This urgent looking and this voice in a smile

for a young man who knows how to die for every dream.

I have no time to look at things,

I almost guess them.

An innate and jealous wisdom

gives me prior glances and sudden trills.

I live on golden margins; I ignore the central joy

of things. I unfold centuries of gold in my being.

And, accelerating gusts—keel or golden wing—,

I make up the sweet time I shall never have.
editorial_note: The translation keeps Pellicer's hurried perception and the odd 'radio' labeling image from the source.

title: Waiting Is Worse Than Being Born...
text:
Waiting is worse than being born,

because only the one who dies

of waiting without making of life

anything but waiting waits. Waiting for you.


And tied to that waiting of yours that wears me down

and wears down your life without bringing you,

here I am dying of anxieties

because this hope fits here, tremendous.


Each day, oh you who are delayed!

without knowing that we are moving farther away,

the irreparable distance is smaller,

of thinking, of waiting, that may distance us.


And here I go on waiting, I attempt nothing

to flee the torment of your waiting.

I no longer know whether outside my life

others remain or not, whether anyone walking remains!


only for you, for when you arrive,

alone, waiting for you, I wait.
editorial_note: The translation keeps Conde's obsessive turns on esperar: waiting, waiting for you, and being consumed by waiting.

title: Still Life
text:
On my daily table, set over the sea,

there are the fish prepared by Alberto

and the fish marinated by Fuensanta.

Wine and bread, with the sweetest delicacy

made in these fields.


Meat does not come to my table here.

The fish that on fragrant embers concentrates

its most joyful juices

feeds my days of dreaming leisure.


My friends keep watch with solicitous care,

offering what is discreet to the palate.

Discreet and wise, perfect knowers

of the Levantine table.


A delicate transmutation of this landscape

is the table that Alberto with Fuensanta

daily fills for me with gifts.


I bite the Mar Menor

and swallow its blood!




The Poems of Mar Menor

, 1959
editorial_note: The translation keeps the table as a transmutation of the Mar Menor landscape, ending in the startling sea-blood image.

title: Tall Red Achiras...
text:
Tall red achiras

—I know with what blood reddened—

in the courtyard of the 5th,

flowering.

Above, in blue sky,

indifferent,

and deaf and mute and blind,

as always.

Below, the prison

and your wounds,

falling drop by drop

on the achiras.

And outside and in us

the seed,

the truth of its strength,

as always.
editorial_note: The translation keeps achiras as the named flower and ties their redness to prison blood and enduring seed.

title: There They Are Without Moorings...
text:
There they are, without moorings,

the infinite ships.

It is a strange voyage

on that sea of screams,

thick and suffocating,

turning like wheels

of a witch's pinwheel,

in that Kafkaesque horror,

in that obtuse absurdity.

Then silence arrives.

A silence that irons

the soul against the floor.


For there everything is silence

when everything is not screaming.
editorial_note: The translation preserves Soler's prison atmosphere: screams, absurdity, then a flattening silence.
